title: Mirrors, Signals & Manoeuvre (MSM/PSL)
whatItIs: The structured routine examiners expect at every junction or hazard: Mirrors, Signal, Manoeuvre, where the manoeuvre itself is Position, Speed, Look.
keyFacts: Use your mirrors in good time before you signal, change direction or change speed.
Mirrors don't cover every area: look round to check the blind spots before you move.
Signal only when it helps other road users (including pedestrians), give it in good time and cancel it after use.
A signal never gives you priority. To stop just after a side road, don't signal until you're passing it.
The national standard asks for a safe, systematic routine such as 'mirrors, signal, manoeuvre, position, speed, look'.
Habitually missing mirror checks can be judged serious: one repeated driving fault can fail a test.

visual.caption: The MSM/PSL routine as DT1 defines it (the 'manoeuvre' is P-S-L)

items.title: M: Mirrors
items.text: Check the mirrors to assess the speed and position of vehicles behind.

items.title: S: Signal
items.text: Signal clearly and in good time, if it would help another road user.

items.title: P: Position
items.text: Position the vehicle correctly and in good time.

items.title: L: Look
items.text: Look for other traffic, assess the situation and act accordingly.

a.label: Driving fault (DT1 examples)
points: Late use of the exterior mirror before changing direction
Signal cancelled before the change of direction was complete

b.label: Serious fault (DT1 examples)
points: No exterior mirror check before a significant change of direction
An essential signal left out when changing direction

onTheTest.question: A pupil turning left checks only the interior mirror, signals and turns. A cyclist was coming up on the left. What should they have done?
options: Checked the left mirror before signalling and watched the left before turning
Signalled earlier and then turned without checking again
Sounded the horn as they started to turn
Checked the mirrors after completing the turn
onTheTest.why: Rule 161: use mirrors in good time before you signal or change direction. Rule 182: watch for traffic coming up on your left before turning left; cyclists may be hidden from view.

onTheTest.question: Your pupil wants to pull up just after a side road on the left. When should they signal left?
options: Well before reaching the side road
As they are passing the side road
Never: a signal is not needed to stop
onTheTest.why: Rule 103: if you want to stop after a side road, don't signal until you are passing it. An earlier signal may suggest you are turning into it.

traps: Signalling isn't automatic: DT1 lists 'signalling unnecessarily' as a fault. Signal when it would help someone.
Mirrors before signal: arriving at a junction and then signalling, or signalling after starting to move, is mistimed.
Looking isn't enough: DT1 records 'using the mirrors but not reacting to the information'.
Never beckon pedestrians or flash headlights to invite others to go: both are faults on test.
